did_you_know.text: Did you know? In chapter 2, Satan appears again among the sons of God, who present themselves before the LORD. This begins Job’s second test.
Did you know? Satan describes his activities with the words, “Roaming throughout the earth and walking back and forth in it”—presenting himself as one who travels throughout the land.

Did you know? The LORD emphasizes that even after all the disasters Job has endured, he still holds firmly to his integrity, calling him “a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil.”
Did you know? In the second test, the LORD allows Satan to afflict Job himself, but sets an explicit limit: “But you must spare his life”—Job’s life may not be taken.
Did you know? Satan afflicts Job with painful sores that cover his body, “from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.”
Did you know? Job uses a piece of pottery to scrape himself and sits among the ashes, a picture that conveys the depth of his suffering and mourning.
Did you know? Job’s three friends are named Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They come together from their homes to sympathize with him and comfort him.
Did you know? When Job’s friends see him from a distance, they do not recognize him. They express their grief by weeping, tearing their clothes, and throwing dust on their heads.

Did you know? Job’s friends sit with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights without speaking because they see that his suffering is very great. Their initial response to his suffering is silence.
